quests.instruction: An orange's juicy inside sections are made up mostly of its sweet, tangy ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This word names the soft, edible part filling most of a fruit's inside.
quests.explanation: Great job! An orange's juicy inside sections are made mostly of its sweet, tangy flesh!
quests.funFact: This juicy part is held together by thin, papery walls inside each little section!

quests.instruction: A coconut's outermost fibrous covering, often used to make rope and mats, is its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This word describes a rough covering that can even be woven into rope.
quests.explanation: You got it! A coconut's outermost fibrous covering, woven into rope and mats, is its husk!
quests.funFact: Rope, mats, and even garden mulch can all be made from this fibrous part!

quests.instruction: Grapes and oranges both have small ___ tucked inside their juicy sections. What word fits?
quests.question: Seed
quests.hint: This is the general word for the tiny bits many fruits carry inside.
quests.explanation: Well done! Grapes and oranges both have small seeds tucked inside their juicy sections, matching this word!
quests.funFact: Some grape varieties have been specially grown to have none of these at all!

quests.instruction: The yellow outer layer you pull off a banana before eating it is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This word names the outer layer you take off with just your fingers, no knife needed.
quests.explanation: Correct! The yellow outer layer pulled off a banana before eating is called its peel!
quests.funFact: For some fruits, like bananas, this outer layer comes off in one easy motion!

quests.instruction: A peach's soft, juicy inside, the part you bite into, is called its ___. Which word names it?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This is the juicy part left once you remove both the fuzzy skin and the hard pit.
quests.explanation: Super! A peach's soft, juicy inside, the part you bite into, is called its flesh!
quests.funFact: This juicy part often turns a deeper color the closer it gets to the pit!

quests.instruction: Pulling an orange apart by hand naturally reveals its separate juicy ___. What word names them?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This word describes the natural divisions a citrus fruit falls into once peeled.
quests.explanation: Nice work! The separate juicy sections revealed by pulling an orange apart are called segments!
quests.funFact: This natural division is exactly why oranges are so easy to share at snack time!

quests.instruction: A coconut's rough, hairy outer layer, covering the hard shell underneath, is called its ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This is the thick, fibrous layer you'd need tools to remove.
quests.explanation: You found it! A coconut's rough, hairy outer layer over its hard shell is called its husk!
quests.funFact: It takes real strength or a sharp tool to remove this tough layer from a coconut!

quests.instruction: A grapefruit is made up of large, juicy ___ held together by a thin white lining. What's the word?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This word names the natural sections a citrus fruit is divided into.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! The large, juicy sections a grapefruit is made up of are called segments!
quests.funFact: Some citrus fruits have as few as eight of these, while others have many more!

quests.instruction: Cherries are small, but they still hide one hard ___ you need to watch out for. What's the word?
quests.question: Pit
quests.hint: This word describes the one hard part hiding inside an otherwise soft, juicy fruit.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! Cherries hide one hard pit you need to watch out for, matching this word!
quests.funFact: Some cherry-pitting tools can remove this hard part in a single quick squeeze!

quests.instruction: A lemon's thick, bumpy outer layer, often grated for its zest, is called its ___. What word names it?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This word describes the outer covering, which can also be finely grated for flavor.
quests.explanation: Terrific! A lemon's thick, bumpy outer layer, grated for zest, is called its peel!
quests.funFact: The tiny oil pockets in this layer are exactly what give grated zest its strong flavor!

quests.instruction: The thin green part connecting a cherry to its branch is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This word names the thin part still attached when you pick a fruit.
quests.explanation: Yes! The thin green part connecting a cherry to its branch is called its stem!
quests.funFact: This part is what keeps a fruit attached to its plant while it's still growing!

quests.instruction: The soft, juicy orange inside of a mango, found between its skin and its pit, is its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This word names the soft, juicy part you actually eat, not the skin or the pit.
quests.explanation: That's right! The soft, juicy orange inside of a mango, between its skin and pit, is its flesh!
quests.funFact: This is the part of a fruit that holds most of its natural sugar and juice!

quests.instruction: A grape stays attached to its bunch by a thin ___. What's the word for this thin part?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This word names the thin connector between a fruit and the rest of its bunch or branch.
quests.explanation: Great job! The thin part connecting a grape to its bunch is called its stem!
quests.funFact: Some fruits, like grapes, have many of these branching off just one bunch!

quests.instruction: Nectarines share the same single hard ___ in their center as a peach does. What word fits?
quests.question: Pit
quests.hint: This is the single tough part your teeth should never bite straight into.
quests.explanation: You got it! Nectarines share the same single hard pit as a peach, matching this word!
quests.funFact: Nectarines and peaches are so closely related that they share almost everything but their skin!

quests.instruction: After eating a pear down to its middle, the seedy part left in your hand is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This is the part most people don't eat, right in the very center.
quests.explanation: Well done! The seedy part left in your hand after eating a pear is called its core!
quests.funFact: This tougher middle part is usually left uneaten because of its firm, seedy texture!

quests.instruction: The green outer part of a watermelon that's often left uneaten is called its ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Rind
quests.hint: This word names a thick outer layer, distinct from the thin peel of a banana.
quests.explanation: Correct! The green outer part of a watermelon often left uneaten is called its rind!
quests.funFact: Unlike a banana's thin peel, this part is usually too tough and bitter to enjoy raw!

quests.instruction: Once all the juicy flesh of a pear is gone, the firm center holding its seeds is its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This is the leftover part in your hand after the fruit is mostly eaten.
quests.explanation: Super! The firm center holding a pear's seeds is called its core!
quests.funFact: Apples, pears, and quinces all share this same seedy center part!

quests.instruction: Each little curved piece you pull from inside a tangerine is called a ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This word describes one single natural section of a peeled citrus fruit.
quests.explanation: Nice work! Each little curved piece pulled from inside a tangerine is called a segment!
quests.funFact: A thin, papery skin usually wraps around each of these individual little pieces!

quests.instruction: Pomegranates are famous for being absolutely packed with hundreds of juicy ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Seed
quests.hint: This word names the small parts that give a pomegranate its crunchy juiciness.
quests.explanation: You found it! Pomegranates are famous for being packed with hundreds of juicy seeds, matching this word!
quests.funFact: A single pomegranate can hold as many as 600 of these juicy little parts!

quests.instruction: Before slicing an orange into wedges, you first pull away its ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This is the part removed by hand, unlike a part that needs to be cut with a knife.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! The part pulled away by hand before slicing an orange into wedges is its peel!
quests.funFact: Removing this part by hand is one of the easiest ways to prepare a fruit!

quests.instruction: Peaches and cherries both have one single hard ___ in the very center. What's the word?
quests.question: Pit
quests.hint: This word names the one big, hard part you should never bite down on.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! Peaches and cherries both have one single hard pit in the center, matching this word!
quests.funFact: This hard part is why peaches and cherries are both called stone fruits!

quests.instruction: The outer layer of a kiwi, which some people choose to eat and others remove, is its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This word names the fuzzy outer covering, whether or not someone chooses to eat it.
quests.explanation: Terrific! The fuzzy outer layer of a kiwi, sometimes eaten and sometimes removed, is its peel!
quests.funFact: Some people eat a kiwi's fuzzy outer layer whole, seeds, peel, and all!

quests.instruction: The soft white inside of a coconut, scraped out and often dried into flakes, is its ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This word names the edible part, distinct from a fruit's hard outer shell.
quests.explanation: Yes! The soft white inside of a coconut, dried into flakes, is its flesh!
quests.funFact: This soft white part can be dried, shredded, or even pressed into coconut milk!

quests.instruction: The tiny green piece left behind after you pull a cherry from its branch is its ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This is the leftover thin part still attached to a fruit after picking.
quests.explanation: That's right! The tiny green piece left after pulling a cherry from its branch is its stem!
quests.funFact: Some people even try tying this thin part into a knot using only their tongue!

quests.instruction: Before eating an orange, you first remove its thick, bumpy ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This is the part you strip away by hand to reach the juicy fruit inside.
quests.explanation: Great job! The thick, bumpy layer removed before eating an orange is called its peel!
quests.funFact: A citrus fruit's outer layer holds tiny pockets of fragrant oil!

quests.instruction: The middle part of an apple, where its seeds are tucked away, is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This word names the center part left behind after you eat all the way around a fruit.
quests.explanation: You got it! The middle part of an apple where its seeds are tucked away is called its core!
quests.funFact: This part is usually tossed away, but it's actually where all the seeds are kept safe!

quests.instruction: Before eating a strawberry, some people first pull off its short, leafy ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This word describes the thin, often leafy part attached to the top of a fruit.
quests.explanation: Well done! The short, leafy part pulled off a strawberry before eating is its stem!
quests.funFact: This part connects a fruit to its plant, carrying water and nutrients while it grows!

quests.instruction: A cantaloupe's netted, tough outer covering that gets tossed away is called its ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Rind
quests.hint: This word names the part that protects a melon but usually isn't eaten.
quests.explanation: Correct! A cantaloupe's netted, tough outer covering that gets tossed away is called its rind!
quests.funFact: That netted pattern on the outside is actually a clue growers use to check ripeness!

quests.instruction: A strawberry's little green cap sits right above its short, leafy ___. What word names this part?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This word describes the thin part that once linked the fruit to its plant.
quests.explanation: Super! The short, leafy part beneath a strawberry's green cap is its stem!
quests.funFact: This part is usually pulled away and tossed before the berry is ever eaten!

quests.instruction: Tomatoes and bell peppers both have small ___ clustered inside, even though people often call them vegetables. What word fits?
quests.question: Seed
quests.hint: This is the everyday word for the tiny parts many fruits carry to make new plants.
quests.explanation: Nice work! Tomatoes and bell peppers both have small seeds clustered inside, matching this word!
quests.funFact: Even foods people call vegetables can be true fruits underneath, seeds and all!
